author: sonnet
label: seeded-01-01
changes: Rewrote the intro to state the whole mechanism in two sentences before the diagram.
Expanded the diagram to show all branches (401, fail-open, 429, allowed) with alt/else, including that Redis is never touched on 401 and that 429s are not forwarded.
Added what the diagram previously left out: key resolution result, 50 ms timeout, backend 500 still counting, and response headers.

Made the design decisions explicit: fixed calendar-minute window with its boundary-burst tradeoff, key format, TTL, atomic check-then-increment so rejects cost nothing, Redis TIME for clock agreement, Retry-After calculation.
Replaced terse fragment notes with full sentences and explained why shared Redis defeats the 6x problem and why per-customer budget covers multiple keys.
Stated that fail-open responses omit X-RateLimit headers, and that 429 does not carry them.
Marked the Enterprise limit visibly as open and noted its consequence for the check instead of picking a number.
Added a short 'How it works' label to the opening paragraph and reworded it so the script's behavior is stated plainly.
Added a note in the diagram showing where the limit comes from, with Standard at 100 per minute and Enterprise visibly marked OPEN, so the open decision is not only in the notes.
Explained that Redis runs a Lua script without interleaving other commands, so a reader unfamiliar with Redis can follow the atomicity claim.
Simplified wording in several notes (Counter key, Window, Retry-After, Fail open) and split long sentences.
Stated the fail-open trade-off (limits unenforced during an outage) as a closing clause.
Defined Redis, atomic script and Lua in plain words for readers new to the stack.
Diagram: the first client message now says the X-Api-Key header may be missing, so the 401 branch makes sense.
Window note: said the 2x overshoot is a short burst, and that old counters are cleaned up automatically.
Limits note: gave examples of what the open Enterprise decision covers and said the diagram shows only the path for a plan that has a limit.
Kept the structure, diagram flow and all requirements unchanged.
